scientific_question: Does a narrowly bounded repair for a single missing closing action tag reduce parser-induced fallback and improve closed-loop WebShop outcomes under the exact H1.30 task/seed/model contract?
hypothesis: The 16 observed malformed completions that contained a closed think tag and a single legal action but omitted only </action> are a runtime-format bottleneck; accepting only that case should reduce invalid attempts without changing the model, prompt, tasks, seeds, or evaluator.

treatment.repair_rule: Only append </action> when the completion has a closed <think>, exactly one opening <action>, no closing action tag, and the suffix is one legal search/click/select/buy[...] action with no nested tag. All other malformed output remains on the existing one-retry/fallback path.

decision_rule: Compare the v2 treatment with the preserved v1 run descriptively; do not change the formal H1.30 capability threshold or promote this diagnostic to a method comparison.
claim_boundary: A parser-contract/runtime diagnostic only. It cannot establish model capability, OpenEvo efficacy, teacher benefit, or OpenEvo-versus-SEED superiority.
